abstract: |
  Theories of third-language (L3) morphosyntactic transfer disagree over whether
  prior-language influence is wholesale or property-by-property, and are silent on
  how it consolidates. We tracked electrophysiological and behavioural signatures of
  three properties (subject--verb gender agreement, differential object marking,
  verb--object number agreement) as Norwegian--English bilinguals acquired
  Mini-English or Mini-Norwegian over four sessions, from the first post-training
  session to post-consolidation retention. Single-trial event-related potential (ERP)
  amplitudes and judgement accuracy were analysed in Bayesian multilevel models
  with informative priors. Gender agreement, whose Mini-Norwegian realisation
  aligns with the learners' first language, produced a grammaticality effect that
  grew with training. In a refit that freed the retention session from that trend,
  the effect at retention did not depart credibly from the trend on average, but the
  two languages diverged credibly, the Mini-English estimate falling below the
  Mini-Norwegian one. Only the group difference is supported. Behaviourally, the
  same property favoured Mini-Norwegian learners, the design's only
  first-language-congruent advantage. Differential object marking yielded a
  transient early effect, a late language-conditioned modulation and a behavioural
  decline at retention. Verb--object number agreement, novel to both prior
  languages, strengthened across the retention interval, and within groups only for
  Mini-Norwegian learners. In whole-scalp decoding, only gender agreement separated
  the conditions on a baseline at chance. Descriptively, no property's pattern
  generalised to another, consistent with property-specific coding. Both novel
  properties showed source-language modulations of opposite sign, unexplained. The
  growth of the gender-agreement advantage across sessions favours a
  property-by-property account over a wholesale one, though one dissociating
  property leaves the conclusion provisional.
keywords: [L3 acquisition, morphosyntactic transfer, ERP, artificial language, Bayesian multilevel models, retention]
bibliography: references.bib
floatsintext: true
author-note:
  correspondence-note: >
    Correspondence concerning this article should be addressed to Pablo Bernabeu,
    Department of Education, University of Oxford, 15 Norham Gardens, Oxford OX2 6PY,

    Madrid, Spain, Email: jgonzalezal@nebrija.es.
format:
  apaquarto-pdf:
    documentmode: man
    pdf-engine: lualatex
    include-in-header:
      - text: |
          % apaquarto's template decrements the table counter at the end of every
          % longtable that carries no caption of its own (apatemplate.tex, "Disable
          % longtable counter"). Quarto now places the caption on an enclosing table
          % float and marks the longtable \def\LTcaptype{none}, so no longtable
          % carries its own caption any more and that decrement cancels the increment
          % the \caption just made. Without this, every table prints as "Table 1" and
          % every cross-reference to a table resolves to 1 -- in the PDF only; the
          % HTML and DOCX outputs number correctly. Restore the lost increment.
          \makeatletter
          \AtBeginDocument{%
            \apptocmd{\endlongtable}{\ifLTpatch@caption\else\addtocounter{table}{1}\fi}{}{}%
          }
          \makeatother

          % --- Vertical rhythm -------------------------------------------------
          % Defaults left captions crowded against their table or figure, opened a
          % gap above and below every display equation that broke the flow of the
          % surrounding sentence, and put more space under a heading than over it,
          % which detaches the heading from the text it introduces.
          % caption.sty is already loaded by the apa7 class, so only its settings are
          % adjusted here; loading it again risks an option clash.
          \captionsetup{aboveskip=10pt, belowskip=10pt}
          % apa7 forces \flushbottom, which stretches the flexible vertical glue
          % between paragraphs when a page happens to end unevenly. In a double-
          % spaced manuscript that can create conspicuous, page-specific gaps in
          % the running text. Keep paragraph spacing stable and let the page bottom
          % remain naturally ragged instead.
          \raggedbottom
          % Keep multi-line displays compact without changing the manuscript's
          % double spacing in ordinary prose.
          \AtBeginDocument{%
            \setlength{\jot}{0pt}%
            \setlength{\abovedisplayskip}{4pt}%
            \setlength{\belowdisplayskip}{4pt}%
            \setlength{\abovedisplayshortskip}{2pt}%
            \setlength{\belowdisplayshortskip}{2pt}%
          }
          % Heading spacing is left to the apa7 class. The titlesec package cannot parse
          % that class's redefined heading levels: it fails at \ttl@extract\subparagraph
          % with 'Argument of \subparagraph has an extra }', and the document does not
          % build with it loaded. The spacing the class applies is APA's own, which is
          % what a journal expects, and the roomy look in manuscript mode comes from the
          % required double spacing rather than from the heading skips.

          % --- Keep wide tables inside the text block --------------------------
          % A table whose natural width exceeds the measure runs into the margin
          % rather than being scaled, and its column headers then collide.
          \usepackage{etoolbox}
          \usepackage{graphicx}
          \usepackage{needspace}
           \AtBeginEnvironment{longtable}{\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}}
          \makeatletter
          \g@addto@macro\@floatboxreset{\centering}
          \makeatother
    # cairo_pdf embeds the fonts it uses and renders the Unicode minus, micro and

    knitr:

```{r setup}
#| include: false
# =============================================================================
# Manuscript setup -- shared paths, results loading, inline-reporting helpers.
# The document is designed to render at ANY stage: before the HPC models exist it
# prints clearly-marked placeholders; once results/_pooled_*.csv are present every
# number, table and figure is populated automatically from those artefacts. This
# "render-anytime" design keeps the manuscript reproducible and prevents stale,
# hand-copied statistics (Marwick, Boettiger & Mullen, 2018,
# https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2017.1375986).
# =============================================================================
# Figure text size, set once and inherited by every figure through les_theme(). Each
# figure is authored at the width of the text block, so nothing is scaled on placement
# and a point here is a point on the page. While several figures were authored at 8
# inches and placed in a 6.5-inch measure, the 9 pt previously set here arrived as
# roughly 7.3 pt, below what is legible in print.
LES_FIG_BASE_SIZE <- 10

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(here)
  source(here::here("_shared", "R", "00_paths.R"))
  source(here::here("_shared", "R", "05_funnel.R"))   # les_funnel(), shared with Paper 2
  source(here::here("paper_1_transfer", "scripts", "_config.R"))
  # les_theme(), les_div, the number formatters, .read_csv_if(), prov(), flow_n() and
  # pstat(), shared with Paper 2 so both manuscripts report by one set of rules.
  source(here::here("_shared", "R", "06_manuscript_helpers.R"))
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  has_knitr <- requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)
  # depictr supplies the figure theme and the colour system for both manuscripts, so
  # the two papers share one visual identity instead of each chunk re-specifying a
  # theme and hand-coding palette hexes. Its default qualitative palette is the
  # colourblind-safe Okabe-Ito set. Optional: if it is unavailable the document falls
  # back to theme_minimal(), consistent with the render-anytime design.
  has_depictr <- requireNamespace("depictr", quietly = TRUE)
  if (has_depictr) {
    library(depictr)
    depictr_options(base_size = LES_FIG_BASE_SIZE)
  }
})

# --- Literature-composition counts (results/_literature_trend.csv, written by
# scripts/10_extract_literature_trend.R via the Scopus API). Injected inline so the
# Introduction's claim about the field's methodological balance carries no
# hand-transcribed number and updates whenever the search is re-run.
lit_n <- function(stratum) {
  if (is.null(.lit_tbl)) return("NN")
  v <- sum(.lit_tbl$n[.lit_tbl$stratum == stratum], na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(v) || v == 0) "NN" else as.character(v)
}
lit_years <- function() {
  if (is.null(.lit_tbl)) return("NN")
  paste0(min(.lit_tbl$year), " and ", max(.lit_tbl$year))
}
lit_ratio <- function() {
  if (is.null(.lit_tbl)) return("NN")
  a <- sum(.lit_tbl$n[.lit_tbl$stratum == "Acceptability/grammaticality judgement"], na.rm = TRUE)
  b <- sum(.lit_tbl$n[.lit_tbl$stratum == "Electrophysiology (ERP/EEG)"], na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(a) || !is.finite(b) || b == 0) return("NN")
  as.character(round(a / b))
}

# Qualitative colour scale for figures that map a discrete variable without a
# fixed, semantically meaningful palette. depictr's default is Okabe-Ito; the
# fallback avoids ggplot2's default hues, whose red/green pairing is the least
# accessible option available.
les_colour <- function(...) {
  if (has_depictr) depictr::scale_colour_depictr(...)
  else ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c("#000000", "#0072B2", "#D55E00"), ...)
}

# --- Load pooled artefacts written by script 05 (if they exist) --------------
.lit_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_literature_trend.csv"))  # see lit_n() below

# Computational provenance recorded at fit time by _shared/R/04_provenance.R, so the
# reported versions are those of the run that produced these results rather than of the
# machine rendering the document. Absent until the pipeline is next run.
# The Methods state that four mis-filtered Session-3 datasets are excluded. That
# claim is about the models reported below, so it is checked against those models:
# scripts 03 and 04 record, for every fit, how many rows of the data they were
# fitted to belonged to a mis-filtered participant-session, and script 05 pools
# those records here. A marker is printed unless every applicable fit reports zero.
#
# An earlier version tested instead for the existence of results/_exclusions.csv,
# which the extraction scripts wrote as a side effect. That was unsound: re-running
# an extraction created the file even when the fitted models being reported were
# older than the exclusion and still contained the four datasets, so the marker
# cleared while the numbers were stale. Keying on the fits themselves cannot fail
# that way.
# --- Which random-effect structure the reported results come from ------------
# "maximal" = crossed by-participant and by-item random effects, each carrying an
# intercept plus grammaticality and session slopes. That is the structure the design
# justifies, since grammaticality varies within both participants and items, and it is
# what the paper reports. "base" is the same model without the by-item grammaticality
# slope, retained and reported as a sensitivity analysis. Every accessor below routes
# through LES_P1_PRIMARY so the two can be swapped in one place rather than by editing
# call sites, and so a half-switched document is impossible.
LES_P1_PRIMARY <- "maximal"
.STRUCT_SUFFIX <- c(maximal = "_itemslope", base = "")

# Resolve a bare ERP cell id to the primary structure's model id. Ids that already
# name a variant explicitly (a weak-prior or common-sample fit, or an already-suffixed
# cell) are returned untouched, so a call site can still reference a specific fit.
.mid <- function(model_id) {
  if (!grepl("^erp_", model_id)) return(model_id)                       # accuracy models
  if (grepl("_(weakprior|itemslope|commonsample)$", model_id)) return(model_id)
  paste0(model_id, .STRUCT_SUFFIX[[LES_P1_PRIMARY]])
}

.fitmeta_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_pooled_fit_metadata.csv"))

# Participants in the fitted ERP models of one property, from the fit records. The
# flow count is taken from the trial-count table, but the models also require the
# L1-dominance covariate, and a participant without that score is dropped by listwise
# deletion, so the modelled N can be one short of the usable-EEG N. It is read from the
# primary structure's informative fits, which all share one N per property.
erp_model_n <- function(property) {
  if (is.null(.fitmeta_tbl)) return("NN")
  m <- .fitmeta_tbl[startsWith(.fitmeta_tbl$model, paste0("erp_", property, "_")) &
                      !grepl("_retfree|_keepmisfiltered", .fitmeta_tbl$model) &
                      .fitmeta_tbl$prior_set %in% "informative", , drop = FALSE]
  if ("structure" %in% names(m)) m <- m[m$structure %in% LES_P1_PRIMARY, , drop = FALSE]
  v <- unique(m$n_participants)
  if (length(v) != 1L || is.na(v)) return("NN")
  as.character(v)
}

# The decision rule lives in les_p1_misfilter_status() (scripts/_config.R), beside the
# helpers it audits, and scripts/test_exclusion_guard.R tests that function directly.
misfilter_status <- function() {
  why <- les_p1_misfilter_status(.fitmeta_tbl, LES_P1_PRIMARY)
  if (nzchar(why)) paste0(" **[Pending: ", why,
                          "; re-run the extraction and model fits to bring the reported",
                          " results into line.]**") else ""
}

.prov_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_provenance.csv"))   # read by prov()
# The decoding job writes its own small provenance record (hpc/08_decoding.slurm), with the
# seed and permutation settings it actually exported. The ERP fitting run's record carries a
# default for the decoding seed that no decoding job set, so the decoding value is read from
# the decoding record and not from the ERP one.
.dprov_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_decoding_provenance.csv"))
prov_dec <- function(component, fallback = "*[value pending a decoding run]*") {
  if (is.null(.dprov_tbl)) return(fallback)
  r <- .dprov_tbl[.dprov_tbl$component == component, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1 || is.na(r$version[1])) return(fallback)
  as.character(r$version[1])
}
conv_tbl      <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_pooled_convergence.csv"))
# Number of fitted models whose id matches a pattern, for the composition sentence in the
# convergence appendix, so the breakdown cannot drift from the injected total.
conv_n <- function(pattern) {
  if (is.null(conv_tbl)) return("NN")
  as.character(sum(grepl(pattern, conv_tbl$model)))
}
post_tbl      <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_pooled_posterior_summaries.csv"))
retention_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_retention_contrasts.csv"))
sens_tbl      <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_prior_sensitivity.csv"))
results_ready <- !is.null(post_tbl)

# --- Raw-data descriptives: participant flow, demographics and ERP trial
# retention, written by scripts 00_extract_participants.R and
# 00c_extract_erp_retention.R. Injected inline so no count, demographic or
# retention figure is transcribed by hand (the drift that leaves the two papers
# disagreeing on a count is thereby impossible).
flow_tbl    <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_sample_flow.csv"))
parts_tbl   <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_participants.csv"))
erp_ret_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_erp_trial_retention.csv"))
gate_tbl    <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_training_gate_flow.csv"))
# Three further descriptives that were typed into the Method until the extraction
# scripts were extended to write them (00_extract_participants.R,
# 00c_extract_erp_retention.R and 02_extract_accuracy.R). Each sentence below prints a
# marked fallback until its artefact exists, so a typed value can never outlive the data.
other_lang_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_participants_other_languages.csv"))
mis_share_tbl  <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_misfiltered_share.csv"))
sent_inv_tbl   <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_sentence_inventory.csv"))

# Languages reported beyond Norwegian and English: how many participants, and the two
# most often named.
other_lang_sentence <- function() {
  n <- pstat("n_other_language", "value", 0)
  if (identical(n, "NN") || is.null(other_lang_tbl) || !nrow(other_lang_tbl)) {
    return(paste0("Some participants also reported knowledge of a further language, most ",
                  "often German or Spanish, which the design did not screen out (see ",
                  "Limitations). *[count pending the participant extraction]*"))
  }
  top <- utils::head(other_lang_tbl$language, 2)
  paste0(n, " of the ", pstat("n_lhq3", "value", 0), " also reported knowledge of at least ",
         "one further language, most often ", paste(top, collapse = " or "), ". Several of ",
         "the languages named mark grammatical gender or case, and the design did not ",
         "screen them out (see Limitations).")
}

# Share of the retained Session 3 trials held by the four mis-filtered datasets, per
# property recorded at that session.
misfilter_share_sentence <- function() {
  if (is.null(mis_share_tbl) || !nrow(mis_share_tbl)) {
    return(paste0("The excluded data amount to roughly 6% of the Session 3 observations in ",
                  "both the gender-agreement and the differential-object-marking analyses ",
                  "*[share pending the retention extraction]*."))
  }
  lab <- LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE
  m <- mis_share_tbl[order(match(mis_share_tbl$grammatical_property, names(lab))), ]
  parts <- sprintf("%s%% for %s", apa_num(m$share_pct, digits = 1),
                   unname(lab[m$grammatical_property]))
  paste0("The excluded datasets hold ", paste(parts, collapse = " and "),
         " of the retained Session ", paste(unique(m$session), collapse = " and "),
         " trials.")
}

# Distinct sentences against judgement trials in the session with most trials, and the
# mean number of presentations per distinct sentence, which is what bears on whether an
# item term is worth carrying.
sentence_inventory_clause <- function() {
  if (is.null(sent_inv_tbl) || all(is.na(sent_inv_tbl$n_distinct_sentences))) {
    return(paste0("The judgement sentences are generated combinatorially, so that each ",
                  "distinct sentence is presented to only a few participants ",
                  "*[inventory pending the accuracy extraction]*."))
  }
  s <- sent_inv_tbl[!is.na(sent_inv_tbl$n_distinct_sentences), ]
  s <- s[which.max(s$n_trials), ]
  sprintf(paste0("The judgement sentences are generated combinatorially. In Session %d, the ",
                 "%s judgement trials of %s participants presented %s distinct sentences, ",
                 "each on average %s times across the sample."),
          as.integer(s$session), formatC(s$n_trials, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
          s$n_participants, formatC(s$n_distinct_sentences, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
          apa_num(s$n_trials / s$n_distinct_sentences, digits = 1))
}

# The sample is described as bilinguals rather than adults because the youngest
# participant was under 18 at the time of the questionnaire. That is a fact about the
# participants, not a rounding artefact: exactly one LHQ3 record gives an age below 18
# (the next lowest is 18), and that person contributes trials to the fitted models. The
# sentence is emitted from the data, so it disappears by itself if the minimum ever rises
# to 18 or above. The guardian-consent clause in the Participants paragraph is
# conditioned on the same test and injects the same minimum.
minors_note <- function() {
  if (is.null(parts_tbl)) return("")
  r <- parts_tbl[parts_tbl$metric == "age_years", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1 || is.na(r$vmin) || r$vmin >= 18) return("")
  paste0(" The youngest participant was under 18 at the time of the questionnaire.",
         " All others were adults.")
}
# Canonical pooled ERP retention (mean / SD trials retained per modelled cell).
erp_ret <- function(field = "mean") {
  if (is.null(erp_ret_tbl) || !"scope" %in% names(erp_ret_tbl)) return("NN")
  r <- erp_ret_tbl[erp_ret_tbl$scope %in% "canonical", , drop = FALSE]
  cand <- intersect(c(field, paste0(field, "_retained")), names(r))
  if (nrow(r) < 1 || !length(cand)) return("NN")
  apa_num(mean(r[[cand[1]]], na.rm = TRUE), digits = if (field == "mean") 1 else 1)
}

# Rejection rate and the grammatical-vs-ungrammatical retention gap, from the
# per-condition rows. Reported so that differential trial loss between the compared
# conditions is shown to be absent rather than merely assumed.
.ret_pc <- function() {
  if (is.null(erp_ret_tbl) || !"scope" %in% names(erp_ret_tbl)) return(NULL)
  d <- erp_ret_tbl[erp_ret_tbl$scope %in% "per_condition_canonical", , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) NULL else d
}
ret_by_gram <- function(level) {
  d <- .ret_pc()
  if (is.null(d) || !"grammaticality" %in% names(d)) return("NN")
  apa_num(mean(d$mean_retained[d$grammaticality == level], na.rm = TRUE), digits = 1)
}
ret_gram_gap <- function() {
  d <- .ret_pc()
  if (is.null(d) || !"grammaticality" %in% names(d)) return("NN")
  g <- mean(d$mean_retained[d$grammaticality == "Grammatical"], na.rm = TRUE)
  u <- mean(d$mean_retained[d$grammaticality == "Ungrammatical"], na.rm = TRUE)
  apa_num(abs(g - u), digits = 2)
}

# --- Multivariate decoding follow-up (scripts 08/09) --------------------------
# The timecourse CSVs carry the cluster-permutation p AND the post-hoc
# within-property Benjamini-Hochberg FDR columns (cluster_p_fdr / significant_fdr);
# the generalisation CSVs hold descriptive cross-language AUC (no permutation null).
# Display labels for plots, from the data manifest (_shared/R/03_data_manifest.R), which
# is the single source of the property order for both manuscripts. Two conventions are
# deliberate.
# (1) ORDER. The properties are listed in the order they were introduced across
#     sessions -- gender agreement (Session 2), differential object marking
#     (Session 3), verb-object number agreement (Session 4) -- and every figure, table
#     and list in the manuscript follows that order. Alphabetical ordering would
#     scramble the design and is never used.
# (2) LITERAL CHARACTERS. These strings are rendered by the graphics device, not by
#     Pandoc, so a LaTeX-style "--" would appear verbatim in the figure. Body-text
#     prose uses the en-dash form (LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE) separately.
.decode_props <- LES_PROPERTY_LABELS
# The same labels for tables, which Pandoc typesets, so the en dash the running text
# uses can be written as "--".
.table_props <- LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE
decode_tc  <- setNames(lapply(names(.decode_props), function(p)
  .read_csv_if(paper1_results(paste0(p, "_decoding_timecourse.csv")))), names(.decode_props))
decode_gen <- setNames(lapply(names(.decode_props), function(p)
  .read_csv_if(paper1_results(paste0(p, "_decoding_generalization.csv")))), names(.decode_props))
decode_ready <- any(!vapply(decode_tc, is.null, logical(1)))

# Permutation count actually used, read back from the decoding artefacts, and the
# resulting floor on an attainable cluster p, 1/(B + 1) (the observed statistic counts
# as one draw from the null; Phipson & Smyth, 2010). Both were previously typed into the
# Methods as "200 shufflings" and ".005", which would silently misdescribe the analysis
# the moment the decoding is re-run at a different B -- as it is being, at B = 1000.
#
# The count is read PER INFERENCE STRATUM, because the two strata can legitimately differ
# while a rerun is in progress. The confirmatory family is the pooled overall time-course,
# so its blocks are the ones whose permutation count governs every cluster-level decision
# the manuscript reports, whereas the exploratory breakdowns enter no family and carry
# their own count. Splitting them lets the Method quote the count behind the reported
# decisions instead of collapsing to a range that describes neither stratum. The fallback,
# for an artefact written before the `inference` column existed, is the analysis label that
# column is derived from.
.n_perm_stratum <- function(confirmatory = TRUE) {
  v <- unlist(lapply(decode_tc, function(d) {
    if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
    sel <- if ("inference" %in% names(d)) d$inference == "confirmatory"
           else d$analysis == "overall"
    d$n_perm[if (confirmatory) sel else !sel]
  }))
  v <- unique(v[is.finite(v)])
  if (!length(v)) NA_integer_ else v
}
.n_perm_conf <- function() .n_perm_stratum(TRUE)
.n_perm_expl <- function() .n_perm_stratum(FALSE)
.n_perm_used <- function() {
  v <- unique(unlist(lapply(decode_tc, function(d) if (!is.null(d)) d$n_perm else NULL)))
  v <- v[is.finite(v)]
  if (!length(v)) NA_integer_ else v
}
# This is spliced into "The permutation null comprised <...> shufflings", so it must stay a
# bare count. Where the exploratory breakdowns lag the confirmatory family, that is
# disclosed by decode_expl_pending() in the following sentence rather than crammed in here.
n_perm_txt <- function() {
  v <- .n_perm_conf()
  if (all(is.na(v))) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  # A confirmatory family still spanning several counts is a half-pulled rerun, and
  # collapsing it to one number would misdescribe the analysis.
  if (length(v) > 1) return(paste0(min(v), "--", max(v), " (mixed; re-run incomplete)"))
  formatC(v, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
}
# The exploratory counts that LAG the confirmatory one, formatted for prose. Empty when
# nothing lags, which is what retires the narrower disclosure.
.n_perm_expl_txt <- function() {
  b <- .n_perm_conf(); e <- .n_perm_expl()
  if (all(is.na(e)) || length(b) != 1L) return("")
  e <- sort(unique(e[is.finite(e) & e < b]))
  if (!length(e)) return("")
  paste(formatC(e, format = "d", big.mark = ","), collapse = " and ")
}
# WHICH properties lag, named for prose. Without this the disclosure reads as though every
# property's breakdowns were affected, when a rerun can leave one property behind and not
# the others. The prose form is used because .decode_props carries the literal hyphen
# the graphics device needs, not the en-dash body text uses.
.n_perm_expl_props <- function() {
  b <- .n_perm_conf()
  if (length(b) != 1L || is.na(b)) return("")
  lags <- vapply(names(.decode_props), function(p) {
    d <- decode_tc[[p]]
    if (is.null(d)) return(FALSE)
    sel <- if ("inference" %in% names(d)) d$inference != "confirmatory"
           else d$analysis != "overall"
    any(d$n_perm[sel] < b, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, logical(1))
  if (!any(lags)) return("")
  nm <- unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[names(.decode_props)[lags]])
  if (length(nm) == 1L) return(nm)
  paste(paste(nm[-length(nm)], collapse = ", "), "and", nm[length(nm)])
}
min_cluster_p <- function() {
  v <- .n_perm_conf()
  if (all(is.na(v)) || length(v) > 1) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  sub("^0", "", formatC(1 / (v + 1), format = "f", digits = if (v >= 500) 4 else 3))
}

# --- Status of the decoding cluster-level inference ---------------------------
# Two disclosures live here, and both are emitted from the artefacts rather than typed, so
# that neither can outlive the state it describes.
#
# The first, decode_provisional(), covers the state the artefacts were in until the
# confirmatory rerun landed: FDR columns written by an earlier revision of
# scripts/09_run_decoding.R, which corrected across ALL of a property's clusters (the pooled
# overall time-course together with the session-resolved and session-by-language
# breakdowns) rather than across the clusters of the pooled overall time-course alone, the
# family the Method describes and the family the current script implements. At B = 200 that
# script also refuses the confirmatory correction outright, because the attainable p-floor
# 1/(B + 1) exceeds the smallest Benjamini-Hochberg threshold the family admits. The notice
# retires itself once every property's CONFIRMATORY rows carry an `inference` column and the
# planned permutation count, which they now do.
#
# The second, decode_expl_pending(), is narrower and is what currently fires: the
# confirmatory family is settled, and only the exploratory breakdowns of the properties
# named by .n_perm_expl_props() still rest on the coarser null while their blocks finish.
# Because those breakdowns enter no correction family, they cannot move a confirmatory
# decision, so this notice qualifies the breakdowns and leaves the decisions standing.
decode_provisional <- function() {
  if (!decode_ready) return(FALSE)
  finalised <- any(vapply(decode_tc, function(d)
    !is.null(d) && "inference" %in% names(d), logical(1)))
  b <- .n_perm_conf()
  !finalised || all(is.na(b)) || any(b < 1000)
}
# Whether the EXPLORATORY breakdowns still rest on a coarser null than the confirmatory
# time-courses. This is a strictly narrower disclosure than decode_provisional(): it leaves
# every reported cluster-level decision standing and qualifies only the breakdowns, which
# enter no correction family and so cannot move a confirmatory decision. It retires by
# itself once the outstanding blocks are pulled back at the confirmatory count.
decode_expl_pending <- function() {
  if (!decode_ready || decode_provisional()) return(FALSE)
  e <- .n_perm_expl(); b <- .n_perm_conf()
  !all(is.na(e)) && length(b) == 1L && any(e < b)
}
decode_status_method <- function() {
  if (!decode_provisional()) {
    if (!decode_expl_pending()) return("")
    return(paste0(
      " One qualification belongs with that description. The confirmatory time-courses ",
      "reported here were corrected under exactly the family just defined, and at the full ",
      "permutation null. The exploratory breakdowns for ", .n_perm_expl_props(), ", which ",
      "enter no family, are still those of an earlier run at ", .n_perm_expl_txt(),
      " shufflings, so their cluster-level $p$ values resolve less finely than the ",
      "confirmatory ones. A rerun that brings them to the same null is under way, and by ",
      "construction it cannot alter a confirmatory decision."))
  }
  paste0(
    " One disclosure belongs with that description. The false-discovery-rate columns in ",
    "the decoding artefacts reported here were written under a wider family than the one ",
    "just defined: correction there ran across all of a property's clusters, the ",
    "session-resolved breakdowns included, rather than across the clusters of its pooled ",
    "overall time-course alone. A rerun of the decoding under the family defined here, ",
    "with a permutation null of 1,000 shufflings, is in progress, and the cluster-level ",
    "decisions reported below are provisional pending it. Which clusters survive depends ",
    "on both the family and the resolution of the null, so those decisions are expected ",
    "to change, most of all where a cluster-level $p$ lies at the attainable floor.")
}
decode_status_appendix <- function() {
  if (!decode_provisional()) {
    if (!decode_expl_pending()) return("")
    return(paste0(
      " The confirmatory decisions reported here rest on the family just defined and on the ",
      "full permutation null. Only the exploratory breakdowns for ", .n_perm_expl_props(),
      " still carry the coarser null of the earlier run, and no decision in the confirmatory ",
      "family depends on them."))
  }
  paste0(
    " The wider family just argued against is nevertheless the one behind the ",
    "false-discovery-rate columns in the artefacts this draft reports, which predate the ",
    "current definition. That is why the cluster-level decoding decisions are labelled ",
    "provisional in the Method and the Results, and it is what the rerun described there ",
    "resolves.")
}
decode_status_transparency <- function() {
  if (!decode_provisional()) {
    if (!decode_expl_pending()) return("")
    return(paste0(
      " One analysis is not yet uniform, and we flag it here as well as where it is",
      "reported. The confirmatory decoding time-courses are final: they are corrected under ",
      "the family the Method describes and rest on the full permutation null. The ",
      "session-resolved breakdowns for ", .n_perm_expl_props(), " are still those of an ",
      "earlier, coarser run, and a rerun that brings them to the same null is in progress. ",
      "Because those breakdowns enter no correction family, the rerun cannot alter a ",
      "confirmatory decision, in either direction."))
  }
  paste0(
    " One analysis is not yet final, and we flag it here as well as where it is",
    "reported. The decoding cluster-level inference rests on artefacts whose ",
    "false-discovery-rate correction spanned a wider family than the Method describes, ",
    "and a rerun under the described family, with a larger permutation null, is in ",
    "progress. Until it lands, no cluster-level decoding decision should be read as ",
    "settled, in either direction.")
}
decode_status_results <- function() {
  if (!decode_provisional()) {
    if (!decode_expl_pending()) return("")
    return(paste0(
      " One qualification attaches to this section. The confirmatory cluster-level decisions ",
      "are final. The session-resolved breakdowns for ", .n_perm_expl_props(), " still rest ",
      "on the earlier, coarser permutation null, so their cluster-level $p$ values resolve ",
      "less finely, and the rerun that will bring them to the same null is still running."))
  }
  paste0(
    " The cluster-level decisions in this section are provisional. As set out under ",
    "*Multivariate decoding* in the Method, the correction family behind the ",
    "false-discovery-rate columns in the present artefacts is wider than the one described ",
    "there, and the permutation null behind them is coarse enough that several ",
    "cluster-level $p$ values sit at the smallest value it can attain. The rerun under the ",
    "confirmatory family will settle which clusters survive. We therefore report the counts ",
    "as the artefacts hold them and draw no conclusion from a property's having none.")
}

# Cross-property generalisation (train on one property's contrast, test on another):
# one CSV per training property, pooled here. Descriptive AUC, no permutation null.
decode_xprop <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(names(.decode_props), function(p)
  .read_csv_if(paper1_results(paste0(p, "_decoding_generalization_crossproperty.csv"))))))
# Peak AUC over all train->test property pairs (NA-safe; "NN" if the stage has not run).
# Restricted to the post-stimulus axis (time_ms >= 0): the maximum of a noisy,
# autocorrelated pre-stimulus AUC time-course carries no information about a violation
# response and would only inflate an apparent effect (see the pre-stimulus control below).
xprop_max <- function(digits = 2) {
  if (is.null(decode_xprop) || !nrow(decode_xprop)) return("NN")
  x <- if ("time_ms" %in% names(decode_xprop)) decode_xprop[decode_xprop$time_ms >= 0, ] else decode_xprop
  apa_num(max(x$auc, na.rm = TRUE), digits = digits)
}

# Per-property decoding summary. Peak AUC and its latency are reported on the
# POST-STIMULUS axis only (time_ms >= 0), because a grammaticality decoder that peaks
# before the critical word is decoding a confound, not a violation response. The
# pre-stimulus interval is retained separately as an explicit negative control
# (mean/peak AUC and the count of FDR-significant pre-stimulus samples), which is
# itself a key diagnostic and is reported in the text. FDR-significant cluster counts
# (whole family and the primary overall time-course) span the full epoch so that any
# pre-stimulus cluster is disclosed rather than hidden.
decode_summary <- function(prop) {
  d <- decode_tc[[prop]]; if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
  has_fdr <- "cluster_p_fdr" %in% names(d)
  cols <- c("analysis", "level", "cluster_id", "cluster_p", if (has_fdr) "cluster_p_fdr")
  cl   <- unique(d[!is.na(d$cluster_id), cols, drop = FALSE])
  ov   <- d[d$analysis == "overall", ]
  post <- ov[ov$time_ms >= 0, ]
  pre  <- ov[ov$time_ms <  0, ]
  peak_i <- if (nrow(post)) which.max(post$auc) else NA_integer_
  g    <- decode_gen[[prop]]
  list(n_fdr         = if (has_fdr) sum(cl$cluster_p_fdr < .05, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_,
       n_overall_fdr = if (has_fdr) sum(cl$cluster_p_fdr < .05 & cl$analysis == "overall", na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_,
       min_clp       = if (nrow(cl)) suppressWarnings(min(cl$cluster_p, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA_real_,
       max_auc_ov    = if (nrow(post)) max(post$auc, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
       peak_ms       = if (!is.na(peak_i)) post$time_ms[peak_i] else NA_real_,
       pre_mean_auc  = if (nrow(pre)) mean(pre$auc, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
       pre_max_auc   = if (nrow(pre)) max(pre$auc, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
       pre_n_fdr     = if (has_fdr && nrow(pre)) sum(pre$significant_fdr %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE"), na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_,
       # Post-stimulus only, for the reason given above: a cross-language AUC peaking
       # before the critical word is not a violation response.
       max_auc_xlang = if (!is.null(g)) {
         gp <- if ("time_ms" %in% names(g)) g[g$time_ms >= 0, , drop = FALSE] else g
         if (nrow(gp)) max(gp$auc, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
       } else NA_real_)
}
dec_gender <- decode_summary("gender_agreement")
dec_dom    <- decode_summary("differential_object_marking")
dec_verb   <- decode_summary("verb_object_number_agreement")

# Inline accessor with a render-anytime placeholder for a not-yet-run decoding.
dec_val <- function(s, field, digits = NA) {
  if (is.null(s) || is.null(s[[field]]) || is.na(s[[field]])) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  if (!is.na(digits)) apa_num(s[[field]], digits = digits) else as.character(s[[field]])
}
# A count and its noun, agreeing in number and spelled out below ten as APA prefers for
# small counts in prose. The alternative, an injected integer beside a typed "cluster(s)",
# leaves a programmer's hedge in the finished sentence.
dec_count <- function(s, field, noun) {
  if (is.null(s) || is.null(s[[field]]) || is.na(s[[field]]))
    return(paste0("*[pending decoding run]* ", noun, "s"))
  n <- as.integer(s[[field]])
  w <- if (n <= 9L) c("no", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven",
                      "eight", "nine")[n + 1L] else as.character(n)
  paste0(w, " ", noun, if (n == 1L) "" else "s")
}

# Largest absolute informative-vs-weak median shift among terms matching `pattern`,
# WITHIN one model family. The families sit on different scales: the ERP response is
# z-scored within participant, whereas the accuracy models are Bernoulli with a logit
# link and their coefficients are log-odds. A single maximum taken across both would be
# a scale-mixed quantity, and describing it as being "on the standardised scale" would
# misreport it -- here it would also inflate the ERP figure roughly seventyfold.
# Rows of the sensitivity table belonging to the primary structure. The table carries
# one comparison per structure, so an unfiltered maximum would report whichever
# structure happened to shift more, not the one the paper reports. Accuracy models have
# only one structure and are always kept.
.sens_primary <- function(tbl) {
  if (!"structure" %in% names(tbl)) {
    # A table written before the structure column existed can only describe the base
    # fits. Reporting its shift while the paper reports the maximal structure would be
    # the same silent mismatch as comparing across two samples, so return nothing and
    # let the caller print its pending marker.
    return(rep(identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "base"), nrow(tbl)))
  }
  # The mis-filter-retained and diversity-covariate refits are sensitivity analyses on
  # other data, so their shifts never enter the reported largest shift.
  (!grepl("^erp_", tbl$model) | tbl$structure %in% LES_P1_PRIMARY) &
    !grepl("_keepmisfiltered|_diversity", tbl$model)
}

# The retention-free refits have no weak-prior counterpart unless one has been pooled;
# the qualification retires itself once _prior_sensitivity.csv carries a retfree row.
retfree_weak_note <- function(tbl = sens_tbl) {
  if (!is.null(tbl) && any(grepl("_retfree", tbl$model))) return("")
  " The retention-free refits were fitted under the informative priors only."
}

prior_shift_max <- function(pattern = "grammaticality", family = "^erp_", tbl = sens_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending sensitivity run]*")
  key <- grepl(pattern, tbl$parameter) & grepl(family, tbl$model) & .sens_primary(tbl)
  if (!any(key)) return("*[pending sensitivity run]*")
  v <- max(abs(tbl$median_shift[key]), na.rm = TRUE)
  # The sentence exists to show the shift is negligible, so keep enough decimals for
  # a negligible value to be legible rather than rounding it to a bare 0.00.
  apa_num(v, digits = if (v < 0.001) 4L else if (v < 0.1) 3L else 2L)
}

# Largest percentage difference between the informative and weak credible-interval
# widths, so the "widths unchanged" claim carries a measured bound rather than an
# assertion.
prior_width_dev <- function(pattern = "grammaticality", family = "^erp_", tbl = sens_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending sensitivity run]*")
  key <- grepl(pattern, tbl$parameter) & grepl(family, tbl$model) & .sens_primary(tbl) &
         is.finite(tbl$ci_width_weak) & tbl$ci_width_weak > 0
  if (!any(key)) return("*[pending sensitivity run]*")
  r <- tbl$ci_width_inf[key] / tbl$ci_width_weak[key]
  apa_num(100 * max(abs(r - 1)), digits = 1)
}

# --- Human-readable labels for the standardised model terms ------------------
.pretty_term <- function(x) {
  x |>
    gsub("^b_", "", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_recoded_grammaticality", "Grammaticality", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_recoded_session", "Session", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_recoded_mini_language", "Language", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_recoded_hemisphere", "Hemisphere", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_recoded_caudality", "Caudality", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_baseline_predictor", "Baseline", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_multilingual_language_diversity", "L1 dominance", x = _) |>
    gsub(":", " x ", x = _)
}

# --- Decimal precision that keeps a credible interval visibly clear of zero ---
# The ERP coefficients are small on the within-participant standardised scale
# (|b| is typically .005-.03), so a fixed two decimals prints an interval that
# genuinely excludes zero as e.g. [-0.02, 0.00] -- typographically identical to one
# that includes it, and so actively misleading about the inference. Widen to as many
# decimals as it takes for the bound nearest zero to show a non-zero digit, capped at
# four. Larger effects are unaffected and still print at two decimals, so precision
# tracks the magnitude being reported rather than being uniform and uninformative.
.les_digits <- function(med, lo, hi,
                        min_d = if (max(abs(c(med, lo, hi)), na.rm = TRUE) < 0.1) 3L else 2L,
                        max_d = 4L) {
  # The rule is simply that no non-zero quantity may print as zero. That matters most
  # for a credible interval, where a "0.00" bound contradicts the credibility claimed
  # for it in the text, but it applies equally to a median, which would otherwise
  # appear as the signed zero "-0.00". The floor is two decimals on the log-odds scale
  # of the accuracy models and three on the within-participant SD scale of the ERP
  # models, whose quantities are an order of magnitude smaller, so a median never prints
  # equal to its own bound; four decimals is the ceiling.
  v <- abs(c(med, lo, hi))
  v <- v[is.finite(v) & v > 0]
  if (!length(v)) return(min_d)
  d <- min_d
  while (d < max_d && round(min(v), d) == 0) d <- d + 1L
  d
}

# Vectorised formatter for tables. Precision is the .les_digits rule applied to the
# whole table (or to each level of `group`, for a table that mixes model families on
# different scales), so that decimals are uniform down a column and a rounded bound
# can be told from a median. Negatives are set with a minus sign, which LaTeX does not
# treat as a break point, so a value is never split as "-" / "0.002".
.fmt_est <- function(med, lo, hi, group = rep(TRUE, length(med))) {
  d <- integer(length(med))
  for (g in unique(group)) {
    k <- which(group == g)
    d[k] <- max(mapply(.les_digits, med[k], lo[k], hi[k]))
  }
  ff <- function(x, k) sub("^-", "-", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = k))
  list(median = mapply(ff, med, d),
       ci     = mapply(function(l, h, k) sprintf("[%s, %s]", ff(l, k), ff(h, k)), lo, hi, d))
}

# --- One pd format for the whole manuscript -----------------------------------
# pd is bounded by 1 like a p value, so the leading zero is dropped (APA 7) and it
# is reported as a proportion everywhere: inline reporters, ranges and tables. It
# previously appeared as a percentage in some places and a proportion in others,
# which invited misreading of borderline values (".95" vs "95"). Values at or
# above .995 keep a third decimal so near-certainty does not round up to 1.00.
.fmt_pd <- function(x) {
  vapply(x, function(v) {
    if (!is.finite(v)) return("NA")
    if (v > 0.9995) return("> .999")
    sub("^0", "", formatC(v, format = "f", digits = if (v >= 0.995) 3 else 2))
  }, "")
}
# Math-mode fragment "p_d = .95" (or "p_d > .999" for the capped case, so the
# relation sign is never doubled after an equals sign).
.pd_math <- function(x) {
  s <- .fmt_pd(x)
  if (startsWith(s, ">")) paste0("p_d ", s) else paste0("p_d = ", s)
}

# --- Inline reporter: "b = m, 95% CrI [lo, hi], pd = .pp" ---------------------
report_effect <- function(model_id, term, tbl = post_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  model_id <- .mid(model_id)          # resolve to the primary structure
  row <- tbl[tbl$model == model_id & tbl$parameter == term, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(row) != 1) return("*[term not found]*")
  d <- .les_digits(row$median, row$ci_low, row$ci_high)
  sprintf("$b = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
          apa_num(row$median, digits = d), apa_num(row$ci_low, digits = d),
          apa_num(row$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(row$pd))
}

# Range of the probability of direction for one term across a set of ERP cells,
# e.g. "between .52 and .87". `model_pattern` is a regular expression selecting the
# cells, so it can pick a property, a window, or both. Injected rather than
# transcribed: both ranges in this manuscript were originally typed by hand, and one
# had silently gone stale by the time the models were refitted -- exactly the drift
# the render-anytime design exists to prevent.
pd_range <- function(term, model_pattern = "^erp_", sep = "and", tbl = post_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  # Restrict to the primary structure. Both structures are pooled into one table and
  # share a cell name up to the suffix, so an unfiltered range would silently span 36
  # fits of 18 cells and report the widest pd across two different models.
  is_max <- grepl("_itemslope$", tbl$model)
  k <- grepl(model_pattern, tbl$model) & !grepl("_weakprior", tbl$model) &
       !grepl("_retfree", tbl$model) & tbl$parameter == term &
       (if (identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")) is_max else !is_max)
  p <- tbl$pd[k]
  if (!length(p)) return("*[term not found]*")
  sprintf("%s %s %s", .fmt_pd(min(p)), sep, .fmt_pd(max(p)))
}

# Median ratio of the credible-interval width WITH the by-item grammaticality slope to
# the width without it, over the ERP cells that have both fits. Injected so the
# robustness claim carries a measured number rather than an assertion that the intervals
# "did not widen much".
itemslope_width_ratio <- function(term = "z_recoded_grammaticality:z_recoded_session:z_recoded_mini_language",
                                  tbl = post_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  k <- tbl$parameter == term & grepl("^erp_", tbl$model) &
       !grepl("_weakprior", tbl$model) & !grepl("_retfree", tbl$model)
  d <- tbl[k, c("model", "ci_low", "ci_high")]
  d$width <- d$ci_high - d$ci_low
  item <- d[grepl("_itemslope$", d$model), ]
  base <- d[!grepl("_itemslope$", d$model), ]
  item$base_model <- sub("_itemslope$", "", item$model)
  m <- merge(item, base, by.x = "base_model", by.y = "model", suffixes = c("_item", "_base"))
  if (!nrow(m)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  apa_num(stats::median(m$width_item / m$width_base), digits = 2)
}

# Number of ERP cells in which `term` is credible, as "k of n". `structure` selects the
# simpler fits ("base") or the maximal by-item ones ("itemslope"), so the manuscript can
# state the sensitivity of a conclusion to the random-effect structure from the artefacts
# rather than by hand.
cred_cells <- function(term, property = "",
                       structure = if (identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")) "itemslope" else "base",
                       tbl = post_tbl) {
  structure <- match.arg(structure, c("base", "itemslope"))
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  # The retention-free refits carry their own suffix and are a third variant of the
  # same cells, not a random-effect structure. They must be excluded from BOTH buckets:
  # "cell_retfree" and "cell_itemslope_retfree" alike fail grepl("_itemslope$"), so
  # without this they would swell the base grid from 18 cells to 42.
  is_item <- grepl("_itemslope$", tbl$model)
  k <- tbl$parameter == term & grepl(paste0("^erp_", property), tbl$model) &
       !grepl("_weakprior", tbl$model) & !grepl("_retfree", tbl$model) &
       (if (structure == "itemslope") is_item else !is_item)
  d <- tbl[k, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  sprintf("%d of %d", sum(d$ci_low > 0 | d$ci_high < 0), nrow(d))
}

# --- Reader-facing labels for the retention tables ----------------------------
# The contrast artefact carries pipeline ids ("erp_gender_agreement_400_900_midline") and
# contrast keys ("within_Mini-Norwegian"). Printed raw they read as variable names, so both
# are mapped here, using the property order every other display item follows. The Measure
# column is not decoration: the two model families sit on different scales (ERP amplitude in
# within-participant SD units, judgement accuracy in log-odds), and a single unlabelled
# Median column invites a cross-scale comparison that is roughly seventyfold wrong.
.retention_labels <- function(d) {
  id     <- sub("^erp_", "", sub("_itemslope", "", sub("_retfree", "", d$model)))
  is_erp <- grepl("^erp_", d$model)
  pkey   <- ifelse(is_erp, sub("_[0-9]+_[0-9]+_(lateral|midline)$", "", id),
                   sub("^accuracy_", "", d$model))
  cmap   <- c(overall = "Overall",
              `within_Mini-Norwegian` = "Mini Norwegian",
              `within_Mini-English` = "Mini English",
              language_difference = "Between languages")
  cl     <- unname(cmap[d$contrast])
  pmap   <- c(gender_agreement = "Gender",
              differential_object_marking = "Object marking",
              verb_object_number_agreement = "Number agreement")
  # Keep ranges and language names together, and use compact reader-facing labels so
  # the Word/PDF tables do not split values in the middle of a row.
  out <- data.frame(
    Property = factor(unname(pmap[pkey]), levels = unname(pmap)),
    `Window (ms)` = ifelse(is_erp,
                           sub(".*_([0-9]+)_([0-9]+)_(lateral|midline)$", "\\1 to \\2", id), "n/a"),
    Region   = ifelse(is_erp,
                      unname(c(lateral = "Lateral", midline = "Midline")[
                        sub(".*_(lateral|midline)$", "\\1", id)]), "n/a"),
    # The note gives the ERP unit; keeping the cell to the short label "ERP" prevents
    # the renderer from putting "(SD)" on a separate line in the narrow measure column.
    Measure  = ifelse(is_erp, "ERP", "Accuracy"),
    Contrast = factor(ifelse(is.na(cl), d$contrast, cl), levels = unname(cmap)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  out
}

report_contrast <- function(model_id, which = "overall", tbl = retention_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  model_id <- .mid(model_id)          # resolve to the primary structure
  row <- tbl[tbl$model == model_id & tbl$contrast == which, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(row) != 1) return("*[contrast not found]*")
  d <- .les_digits(row$median, row$ci_low, row$ci_high)
  sprintf("$\\Delta = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
          apa_num(row$median, digits = d), apa_num(row$ci_low, digits = d),
          apa_num(row$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(row$pd))
}

# --- Between-language difference in a retention gain --------------------------
# Script 05 derives a "language_difference" contrast (Mini-Norwegian minus
# Mini-English retention change) so that any statement about the two languages'
# similarity cites an estimated quantity with its own uncertainty. Until the
# queued summaries run adds that row to _retention_contrasts.csv, the two
# within-language medians are printed with a visible marker instead, in the
# style of misfilter_status().
ret_lang_diff <- function(model_id = "erp_gender_agreement_400_900_midline",
                          freed = FALSE) {
  if (is.null(retention_tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  mid <- paste0(.mid(model_id), if (freed) "_retfree" else "")
  r <- retention_tbl[retention_tbl$model == mid &
                       retention_tbl$contrast == "language_difference", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) == 1) {
    d <- .les_digits(r$median, r$ci_low, r$ci_high)
    return(sprintf(
      "Mini-Norwegian minus Mini-English $\\Delta = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
      apa_num(r$median, digits = d), apa_num(r$ci_low, digits = d),
      apa_num(r$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(r$pd)))
  }
  w <- retention_tbl[retention_tbl$model == mid &
                       grepl("^within_", retention_tbl$contrast), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(w) < 2) return("*[contrast not found]*")
  paste0("within-language medians of ",
         apa_num(w$median[w$contrast == "within_Mini-Norwegian"], digits = 3), " and ",
         apa_num(w$median[w$contrast == "within_Mini-English"], digits = 3),
         "; *[between-language difference contrast pending the queued summaries run]*")
}

# --- Language modulation at the property's first session ----------------------
# With session standardised, the grammaticality x language coefficient is the
# source-language advantage at the AVERAGE session; whether the advantage was
# already present when the property was first probed is the quantity that separates
# transfer standing ready from the start from an advantage accruing with exposure.
# Script 05 derives it from the accuracy draws (b_gl + z_first * b_gsl) and writes
# results/_first_session_language_advantage.csv; reported from that artefact, with
# a visible marker until the queued summaries rerun lands.
first_adv_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_first_session_language_advantage.csv"))
first_sess_adv <- function(model_id = "accuracy_gender_agreement") {
  if (is.null(first_adv_tbl)) {
    return("*[first-session contrast pending the queued summaries run]*")
  }
  r <- first_adv_tbl[first_adv_tbl$model == model_id, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1) return("*[first-session contrast not found]*")
  d <- .les_digits(r$median, r$ci_low, r$ci_high)
  sprintf("$b = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
          apa_num(r$median, digits = d), apa_num(r$ci_low, digits = d),
          apa_num(r$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(r$pd))
}

# --- Retention-free contrasts: reporters and cell tallies ---------------------
# retfree_contrast() returns NULL when the freed fits are absent; retfree_val()
# wraps it for inline use. retfree_tally() counts, across a property's six cells,
# how many freed contrasts are credible (interval excludes zero) or share a sign,
# so statements like "positive in every cell" are computed rather than typed.
retfree_val <- function(cell_id, which = "overall") {
  est <- retfree_contrast(cell_id, which)
  if (is.null(est)) "*[retention-free contrast pending]*" else est
}
.retfree_rows <- function(property, contrast) {
  if (is.null(retention_tbl)) return(NULL)
  want_item <- identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")
  m <- retention_tbl
  k <- startsWith(m$model, paste0("erp_", property, "_")) &
       grepl("_retfree", m$model) & !grepl("_weakprior|_keepmisfiltered", m$model) &
       (grepl("_itemslope", m$model) == want_item) & m$contrast == contrast
  r <- m[k, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(r)) NULL else r
}
retfree_tally <- function(property, contrast,
                          what = c("credible", "positive", "negative")) {
  what <- match.arg(what)
  r <- .retfree_rows(property, contrast)
  if (is.null(r)) return("*[pending]*")
  n <- switch(what,
              credible = sum(sign(r$ci_low) == sign(r$ci_high)),
              positive = sum(r$median > 0),
              negative = sum(r$median < 0))
  .word <- function(i) c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six",
                         "seven", "eight", "nine")[i + 1L]
  tot <- nrow(r)
  if (n == 0L)   return(paste0("none of the ", .word(tot)))
  if (n == tot)  return(paste0("every one of the ", .word(tot)))
  paste0(.word(n), " of the ", .word(tot))
}

# --- Retention-free refit: conditional status ---------------------------------
# LES_P1_RETENTION_FREE=1 refits a cell with an explicit Session-6 offset, so the
# linear term carries the training trend and the offset the deviation at retention
# (scripts/03_fit_brms_erp.R). Script 05 writes those contrasts into
# _retention_contrasts.csv under model ids tagged "_retfree". The consolidation
# reading in the Discussion depends on whether that refit has landed, so the
# sentence is emitted from the artefact rather than typed: once the retfree rows
# are present the freed offset is reported; until then the provisional
# linear-derivation reading is printed with a visible marker, mirroring
# misfilter_status(). The variant exists for gender agreement and differential
# object marking only: verb-object number agreement is sampled at the two
# bracketing sessions, so its linear term already is the retention change and a
# freed offset is not identifiable (script 03 refuses it).
retfree_contrast <- function(cell_id, which = "overall") {
  if (is.null(retention_tbl)) return(NULL)
  want_item <- identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")
  m <- retention_tbl
  k <- startsWith(m$model, cell_id) & grepl("_retfree", m$model) &
       !grepl("_weakprior|_keepmisfiltered", m$model) &
       (grepl("_itemslope", m$model) == want_item) & m$contrast == which
  r <- m[k, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1) return(NULL)
  d <- .les_digits(r$median, r$ci_low, r$ci_high)
  sprintf("$\\Delta = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
          apa_num(r$median, digits = d), apa_num(r$ci_low, digits = d),
          apa_num(r$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(r$pd))
}
retfree_sentence <- function(cell_id = "erp_gender_agreement_400_900_midline") {
  est <- retfree_contrast(cell_id)
  if (!is.null(est)) {
    return(paste0(
      "A refit in which the retention step is free to differ from the training steps ",
      "separates the two readings. For this cell the freed Session-6 offset, the ",
      "deviation at retention, is ", est, "."))
  }
  paste0(
    "Separating an offline gain from continued improvement requires a model in which ",
    "the retention step is free to differ from the training steps. Such a refit is in ",
    "progress for gender agreement and differential object marking (for verb--object ",
    "number agreement, sampled at the two bracketing sessions only, the linear term ",
    "already is the direct contrast), and until its contrasts are pooled we treat ",
    "consolidation as the more plausible of two readings the linear derivation cannot ",
    "adjudicate. **[Pending: retention-free refit contrasts not yet in the pooled ",
    "summaries; re-run script 05 once the refit completes.]**")
}

# --- RSVP timing census -------------------------------------------------------
# scripts/01b_extract_rsvp_timing.R takes a census of ALL presented critical-word
# trials in the raw presentation logs, before any EEG-side exclusion: trial count, the
# distribution of the next word onset after the critical word, and the per-trial count
# of onsets within 900 ms. It writes the scalar fields (n_trials, next_onset_min_ms,
# next_onset_max_ms, next_onset_median_ms, max_onsets_within_900ms) and the per-session
# counts (n_trials_s<session>) as one row of the tracked results/_rsvp_timing.csv, and
# the full census to data_derived/rsvp_timing_overlap.rds, which is not tracked. The
# CSV is read first, as a list so that rsvp_tim() indexes it by field, and the rds is
# the fallback for a checkout that predates the CSV. Injected so the Procedure's timing
# claims track the logs rather than a hand-typed number (the typed median had already
# drifted by 1 ms from the full-census value).
.rsvp_tim <- local({
  csv <- paper1_results("_rsvp_timing.csv")
  if (file.exists(csv)) {
    as.list(utils::read.csv(csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[1, , drop = FALSE])
  } else {
    p <- paper1_derived("rsvp_timing_overlap.rds")
    if (file.exists(p)) readRDS(p) else NULL
  }
})
rsvp_tim <- function(field, big = FALSE) {
  if (is.null(.rsvp_tim) || is.null(.rsvp_tim[[field]]) || !is.finite(.rsvp_tim[[field]]))
    return("*[pending timing extraction]*")
  formatC(.rsvp_tim[[field]], format = "d", big.mark = if (big) "," else "")
}

# --- Response-time screen on the judgement trials -----------------------------
# results/_accuracy_rt_screen.csv records the bounds of the plausibility filter
# the accuracy extraction applies and its cost in trials, so the disclosure in
# the Method is injected rather than typed.
.rt_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_rt_screen.csv"))
rt_screen <- function(field, digits = 0) {
  if (is.null(.rt_tbl) || !field %in% names(.rt_tbl)) return("NN")
  v <- .rt_tbl[[field]][1]
  if (!is.finite(v)) return("NN")
  if (digits > 0) apa_num(v, digits = digits)
  else formatC(v, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
}

# Session 4 logfiles the accuracy extraction cannot read (results/_accuracy_input_gaps.csv,
# a census script 02 writes without changing what it extracts). Two export formats are
# affected, and the participants concerned contribute no Session 4 judgements.
.gap_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_input_gaps.csv"))
acc_gap_sentence <- function() {
  if (is.null(.gap_tbl)) {
    return(paste0("Two features of the Session 4 logs removed further judgements before ",
                  "that screen *[counts pending the accuracy extraction]*."))
  }
  n_of <- function(reason) length(unique(.gap_tbl$participant_lab_ID[.gap_tbl$reason == reason]))
  # Counts below ten are spelled out, as APA 7 asks of counts in running text.
  num_word <- function(n) {
    if (n >= 1 && n <= 9) c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven",
                            "eight", "nine")[n] else format(n, big.mark = ",")
  }
  sprintf(paste0(
    "Two features of the Session 4 logs removed further judgements before that screen. ",
    "The runs of %s participants were exported in two files whose names the extraction's ",
    "file pattern does not match, and the logs of %s participants were exported with a ",
    "semicolon delimiter that the comma-delimited reader cannot parse. Those participants ",
    "contribute no Session 4 judgements and enter the models through their other sessions ",
    "only."), num_word(n_of("split_export")), num_word(n_of("semicolon_delimited")))
}

# --- Extents of the FDR-surviving clusters in a pooled decoding time-course ---
# Typed cluster extents would go stale the moment the decoding is re-run (the
# B = 1000 rerun can shift cluster boundaries), so they are read back from the
# artefact. Returned in temporal order.
dec_fdr_spans <- function(prop) {
  d <- decode_tc[[prop]]
  if (is.null(d) || !"cluster_p_fdr" %in% names(d)) return(character(0))
  ov <- d[d$analysis == "overall" & !is.na(d$cluster_id) &
            !is.na(d$cluster_p_fdr) & d$cluster_p_fdr < .05, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(ov)) return(character(0))
  sp <- lapply(split(ov$time_ms, ov$cluster_id), range)
  sp <- sp[order(vapply(sp, `[`, 0, 1))]
  vapply(sp, function(x) sprintf("%s to %s ms", round(x[1]), round(x[2])), "")
}
dec_span <- function(prop, i) {
  s <- dec_fdr_spans(prop)
  if (length(s) < i) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  s[i]
}
# Smallest cluster-level p across every analysis of one property, formatted as a
# p value (leading zero dropped).
dec_min_p <- function(s) {
  if (is.null(s) || is.null(s$min_clp) || is.na(s$min_clp)) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  paste0("$p = ", sub("^0", "", formatC(s$min_clp, format = "f", digits = 3)), "$")
}
# Whether that smallest cluster-level p sits exactly at the permutation floor 1/(B + 1).
# A p at the floor is indistinguishable from any smaller value, so a null resting on it
# reports the resolution of the null as much as it reports the data. Emitted from the
# artefact so the clause disappears by itself once a larger null separates the two.
dec_at_floor <- function(s) {
  b <- .n_perm_conf()
  if (is.null(s) || is.null(s$min_clp) || is.na(s$min_clp) ||
      all(is.na(b)) || length(b) > 1) return("")
  if (!isTRUE(all.equal(unname(s$min_clp), 1 / (b + 1)))) return("")
  ", which is the smallest value the permutation null can return"
}
# How many clusters of a property's pooled overall time-course sit at that floor. Counted
# from the artefact so the disclosure tracks the run rather than a typed recollection.
dec_n_at_floor <- function(prop) {
  d <- decode_tc[[prop]]; b <- .n_perm_conf()
  if (is.null(d) || all(is.na(b)) || length(b) > 1) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  ov <- unique(d[d$analysis == "overall" & !is.na(d$cluster_id),
                 c("cluster_id", "cluster_p"), drop = FALSE])
  n <- sum(abs(ov$cluster_p - 1 / (b + 1)) < 1e-9, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n > 9L) return(as.character(n))
  c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight",
    "nine")[n + 1L]
}

# --- Render-time guard for prose that names WHICH cells are credible ----------
# cred_cells() injects the count of credible cells, but sentences also describe
# their location ("both on the midline", "every one of those cells is lateral").
# A refit can change the credible set while those words stand, a drift invisible
# at render time. This guard compares the credible set against the cells the
# sentence names and prints a visible marker on any mismatch, mirroring
# misfilter_status().
cred_cells_guard <- function(term, expected, property = "",
                             structure = if (identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")) "itemslope" else "base",
                             tbl = post_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("")
  # Same bucketing rule as cred_cells(): the retention-free refits belong to neither
  # structure, so they are excluded before the base/maximal split.
  is_item <- grepl("_itemslope$", tbl$model)
  k <- tbl$parameter == term & grepl(paste0("^erp_", property), tbl$model) &
       !grepl("_weakprior", tbl$model) & !grepl("_retfree", tbl$model) &
       (if (structure == "itemslope") is_item else !is_item)
  d <- tbl[k, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) return("")
  got <- sort(sub("_itemslope$", "", d$model[d$ci_low > 0 | d$ci_high < 0]))
  if (identical(got, sort(unique(expected)))) return("")
  paste0(" **[Check: the credible set for this term is now {",
         paste(got, collapse = ", "),
         "}; the surrounding sentence names a different set and must be updated.]**")
}
```

When multilingual speakers add a third or later language (L3/Ln), the grammars they
already command shape how its morphosyntax is represented and processed. How that prior knowledge is
recruited is the central question dividing contemporary models of L3
morphosyntactic transfer. Wholesale-transfer accounts hold that a single
previously acquired grammar is selected as the basis for the initial L3 grammar,
whether on typological grounds [the Typological Primacy Model: @rothman2011;
@rothman2015] or because the second language enjoys a privileged cognitive status
[the L2 Status Factor: @bardel2007; @falk2011]. Property-by-property accounts
predict instead that transfer is selective and incremental, with individual
structures transferred (and, where helpful, "enhanced") one at a time as the
learner detects structural similarity. The Linguistic Proximity Model
[@westergaard2017; @westergaard2021; @westergaard2023], the Scalpel Model
[@slabakova2017] and the Cumulative-Enhancement Model [@flynn2004] all take that form.
The wholesale position has recent defenders who raise conceptual and empirical objections
to selective transfer [@schwartzsprouse2021], and initial-stage evidence from early
Catalan--Spanish bilinguals, whose performance on four properties was compatible with
Catalan as the single source of their initial English grammar, has been read as support
for it [@gonzalezalonso2021]. Any test that discriminates between them requires (a) multiple, independently
manipulable grammatical properties, (b) a source language whose relationship to each
property is controlled, and (c) a temporal window long enough to watch transfer emerge
and to test whether what transferred is retained.

## Electrophysiology of morphosyntactic processing

Event-related potentials (ERPs) provide a millisecond-resolution index of how the
brain responds to grammatical violations and are therefore well suited to
revealing the representations that underlie transfer before they surface in overt
behaviour. Most evidence on L3 morphosyntactic transfer has come from offline, untimed
acceptability judgements [@puigmayenco2020; @skalba2026]. These index the outcome of
learning. They leave untouched the moment-to-moment processing that ERPs expose
[@angelovska2023; @rothmanalemanbanon2015]. A single-trial ERP design therefore tests
directly whether source-language structure modulates online comprehension. Online
evidence has begun to appear. Eye-tracking in early learners of Norwegian shows
facilitative and non-facilitative influence from each prior language on different
properties [@skalba2026]. The imbalance is visible in the literature itself
(@fig-literature). In all,
`r lit_n("All L3-transfer research")` records on L3 transfer were indexed between
`r lit_years()`. Of those, `r lit_n("Acceptability/grammaticality judgement")` used
acceptability or grammaticality judgements and `r lit_n("Electrophysiology (ERP/EEG)")`
used electrophysiology, a ratio of roughly `r lit_ratio()` to one. The field has grown steadily while its
electrophysiological base has not.

```{r}
#| label: fig-literature
#| fig-cap: "Methodological Composition of the L3 Morphosyntactic-Transfer Literature Indexed in Scopus, by Publication Year"
#| apa-note: "The upper line is all L3-transfer research. The lower two are the subsets whose title, abstract or keywords mention acceptability or grammaticality judgements, and electrophysiology (ERP/EEG). The counts index relative composition and are not an exhaustive census: Scopus under-covers books and chapters, keyword matching errs in both directions, and records indexed late may still be added for the most recent years. The retrieval queries are recorded in the project repository."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.0
lit_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_literature_trend.csv"))
if (!is.null(lit_tbl)) {
  lt <- lit_tbl
  lt$stratum <- factor(lt$stratum, levels = c(
    "All L3-transfer research", "Acceptability/grammaticality judgement",
    "Electrophysiology (ERP/EEG)"))
  ggplot(lt, aes(year, n, colour = stratum, linetype = stratum)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) + geom_point(size = 0.9) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2005, 2025, 5)) +
    les_colour() +
    labs(x = "Publication year", y = "Records indexed", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
    les_theme() + theme(legend.position = "top") +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
           linetype = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
} else {
  cat("*Literature-composition figure will appear once `_literature_trend.csv` is present (run `scripts/10_extract_literature_trend.R`; needs a Scopus API key).*")
}
```
Three components are relevant here. The left-anterior negativity (LAN) is often linked to
automatic morphosyntactic agreement checking. The N400, a negativity sensitive to
lexical--semantic and thematic integration [@frisch2001; @nieuwland2013], also marks the
early stages of morphosyntactic learning, before a late positivity emerges with rising
proficiency [@osterhout2006]. That later positivity is the P600, first reported for words
inconsistent with the preferred syntactic analysis [@osterhout1992]. Over
centro-posterior sites, it has since been associated with syntactic reanalysis and repair,
and with the late integration of syntactic and semantic information
[@friederici2002tics; @friederici2002pnas]. These map onto the three latency windows
analysed here (200--500, 300--600 and 400--900 ms). Training studies show that the brain's response to
second-language violations becomes more native-like as proficiency increases
[@morganshort2012], and again across a consolidation
interval containing no further exposure [@morganshort2012plos], with negativities and
P600s emerging or shifting over time. Native speakers [@tanner2014] and learners
[@tanner2013] also differ systematically from one another in whether they recruit a more
negativity-dominated or a more P600-dominated response. Artificial-language paradigms, in
which the input is fully controlled, have been particularly valuable for isolating
these dynamics from the confounds of natural-language exposure
[@gonzalezalonso2020; @friederici2002pnas]. Bilinguals learning such a language show a
P600 to syntactic violations at a lower proficiency than monolinguals do [@grey2018].

The closest antecedent to the present design is the artificial-language L3 ERP work of
@gonzalezalonso2020. Its findings shape both our predictions and our reading of the
results, so we set them out in full. Fifty first-language-Spanish, second-language-English
bilinguals were given implicit training on one of two miniature languages, built on
English and Spanish lexicons, and their ERPs to gender-agreement violations were recorded
at first exposure. They named their two languages after those lexicons, and we refer to
their groups by lexicon throughout, so that neither is confused with our own Mini-English
and Mini-Norwegian conditions. The two groups responded differently. In their
English-lexicon language, violations elicited an early (200--500 ms) fronto-lateral
negativity, confined to electrodes in the right-anterior region and followed by nothing in
later windows. In their Spanish-lexicon language, they elicited a broadly distributed
positivity at 300--600 ms. Neither group produced a P600 or
any other canonical index of grammatical processing. The authors read the between-group
difference as differential allocation of attention, driven by each miniature language's
lexical similarity to a prior grammar, and therefore as a precursor of source selection,
not as grammatical processing itself. The present study extends that logic in
three ways. It goes beyond first exposure, tracking each property across up to four
sessions, and it manipulates three properties whose relation to the prior grammars
differs within the same learners. It also closes with an unrehearsed retention test
after months without exposure, so the durability of what transferred can be measured.
Whether the initial-exposure pattern of @gonzalezalonso2020 reappears under these
conditions is itself an empirical question, taken up in the Discussion.

Two behavioural studies share more of the present materials. Each trained speakers on a
miniature language with a Norwegian lexicon and a case system, a property Norwegian
lacks. Prior knowledge of a case language eased acquisition even though the lexicon
pointed to Norwegian, but only where that language and the miniature language marked case
in the same overt form, on the noun [@mitrofanova2023; @castle2026]. Greek, which marks
case on the determiner, gave no such advantage in the first study, and the second found
the advantage subject to word-order bias and proficiency. The overt realisation of a
property conditioned its transfer, and the present gender manipulation varies exactly
that realisation between the two miniature languages. Recent syntheses of the transfer
literature draw attention to the methodological choices that constrain what its findings
can show [@puigmayenco2020; @rothman2019; @gonzalezalonso2026], and longitudinal and
electrophysiological evidence remains among its scarcest. An ERP successor to
@gonzalezalonso2020 trained heritage and second-language bilinguals on a Latin
mini-grammar and found violation responses that no current model had predicted, an
outcome its authors took as a question about the paradigm itself [@pereirasoares2022].
The recurring objection to miniature languages is that a
grammar acquired in hours may not engage the mechanisms of natural morphosyntax. This
literature answers it with the finding that artificial-language learners, once
sufficiently proficient, show qualitatively native-like violation responses
[@morganshort2012; @friederici2002pnas]. What the design buys in exchange is exact
control over every learner's input history, which no natural-language design can offer.

## The present study

We exploit a controlled artificial-language design to test predictions that separate
wholesale from property-by-property transfer, and to characterise the time course
of transfer from the first post-training session through post-training retention.
Norwegian--English bilinguals (first language Norwegian, second language English) acquired
one of two miniature languages, Mini-English or Mini-Norwegian. Within each language, we
manipulated three morphosyntactic properties that vary in their relationship to the
learners' existing grammars: subject--verb gender agreement, differential object marking
and verb--object number agreement. The two languages share their morphemes but differ in
how they realise each property. Mini-Norwegian expresses gender agreement
through a suffixed determiner, as Norwegian does, whereas Mini-English uses an English-like
free determiner. The same property therefore aligns with the first language for one
group only (see Method).

Single-trial ERPs and grammaticality judgements were collected across four
laboratory sessions (Sessions 2, 3, 4 and 6) that trace the learning trajectory
from the first post-training session to a post-consolidation retention test. The properties
enter the design at different points (gender agreement from Session 2,
differential object marking from Session 3 and verb--object number agreement from
Session 4), yielding a cumulative, property-by-property exposure schedule (@fig-design).

```{r}
#| label: fig-design
#| fig-cap: "Exposure and Measurement Schedule"
#| apa-note: "Each grammatical property enters at a different session and recurs thereafter, and the four ERP/behavioural sessions are 2, 3, 4 and 6. Gender agreement therefore has four sessions of coverage, differential object marking three, and verb--object number agreement two. The session axis is ordinal, so equal spacing does not imply equal elapsed time. Sessions 2 to 4 are one week apart, whereas Session 6, the unrehearsed retention test, follows Session 4 after about four months without exposure. The intervals are therefore annotated numerically."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 2.9
.props <- unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS)
.entry <- c(2, 3, 4)
.sess  <- c(2, 3, 4, 6)
design <- expand.grid(s = .sess, p = seq_along(.props))
```
