# Analytic decisions in detail {#apx-analytic-decisions-in-detail}

This appendix sets out the reasoning behind two analytic choices that the Method states
but does not argue in full: the retention of the by-item grammaticality slope in the ERP
models, and the definition of the false-discovery-rate correction family for the
decoding analyses.

## The by-item grammaticality slope

The reason for keeping the by-item grammaticality slope is that dropping it would bias the
test in the direction of the hypothesis. @barr2013 show that omitting random-effect
structure that is present in the population inflates the Type I error rate. They add that,
for within-items manipulations specifically, an intercept-only by-item structure can inflate
it severely, whatever method is used to obtain $p$-values or intervals. Grammaticality is a
within-item manipulation here, so an item term carrying only an intercept and a session
slope is exactly that case for the effect under test.

@matuschek2017 argue the other side: a maximal model can cost power, and they recommend
reducing to a structure the data support. We report the maximal structure nonetheless, for
two reasons. Their argument is that a maximal structure the data do not support costs power, a
result they establish in simulations of models that converge, so it does not turn on
convergence failure. They themselves note that maximal models usually do converge when
fitted in a Bayesian framework such as Stan, while explicitly leaving open whether
fitting overparameterised maximal models makes sense there. Ours converged, meeting the
same criteria as every other
model reported here. We also fit the whole grid a second time without the
by-item grammaticality slope, so a reader can see which conclusions depend on it. That
comparison follows.

## Sensitivity to the by-item grammaticality slope

To show what the maximal structure buys, we refitted the whole grid without the by-item
grammaticality slope, the structure a design in which grammaticality varied only within
participants would have justified. All eighteen cells met the same convergence criteria
under both. The consequence differs sharply between the interaction terms and the main
effect, so we separate them.

The transfer conclusions do not depend on the choice. The interaction is credible for
differential object marking and verb--object number agreement under both structures, and
its intervals are essentially identical in width (`r itemslope_width_ratio()` times the
simpler structure's width at the median). The maximal structure is in fact the more
generous of the two here, since one further cell reaches credibility under it
(differential object marking, 300--600 ms
lateral)`r cred_cells_guard("z_recoded_grammaticality:z_recoded_session:z_recoded_mini_language", c("erp_differential_object_marking_400_900_lateral", "erp_verb_object_number_agreement_400_900_lateral"), structure = "base")`. The count is
`r cred_cells("z_recoded_grammaticality:z_recoded_session:z_recoded_mini_language", structure = "itemslope")`
cells against
`r cred_cells("z_recoded_grammaticality:z_recoded_session:z_recoded_mini_language", structure = "base")`
without the slope.

The grammaticality main effect is a different matter, and it is where the simpler
structure would have misled. Posterior medians barely move between the two, but the
maximal structure's intervals are about
`r itemslope_width_ratio("z_recoded_grammaticality")` times as wide as the simpler
structure's, and that widening is enough to change how many cells clear the credibility
threshold. For gender agreement, the count is
`r cred_cells("z_recoded_grammaticality", "gender_agreement", "itemslope")` cells under
the maximal structure against
`r cred_cells("z_recoded_grammaticality", "gender_agreement", "base")` without the slope,
and, for differential object marking,
`r cred_cells("z_recoded_grammaticality", "differential_object_marking", "itemslope")`
against `r cred_cells("z_recoded_grammaticality", "differential_object_marking", "base")`.
By-item variability in the grammaticality response is therefore not negligible in these
data. Had we reported the simpler structure, we would have described the gender-agreement
grammaticality effect as credible across nearly the whole grid. Under the structure the
design justifies, it keeps its sign and magnitude but is credible in a minority of
cells. The structure-dependent claim is therefore how widely the effect is distributed,
while the existence and direction of the effect hold under both.

## The Session 3 filter exclusion

The Method excludes the Session 3 recordings of four participants, which were high-pass
filtered at 1 Hz where every other recording was filtered at 0.1 Hz. We did not assess
whether these participants' data look unusual, and the exclusion does not rest on that.
It rests on the setting itself, which is a documented generator of artefacts in this kind
of paradigm. Filtering data from a syntactic- and semantic-violation experiment at
cutoffs of 0.3 Hz and above introduces spurious deflections of opposite polarity
immediately before the true N400 and P600 effects [@tanner2015], and 1 Hz lies well
inside that range. The general principle, that a high-pass cutoff must be matched to the
analysis window because an inappropriate one generates artefactual slow deflections, is
set out by @widmann2015. Because the exclusion follows from the filter's known
behaviour, and nothing observed in these participants bore on it, it is not a
results-contingent choice.

## The decoding correction family

The Method states how the second layer of multiplicity control on the decoding analyses
is defined. Correcting instead across the pooled, per-session and
per-session-by-language cells of one property would span nested, overlapping re-analyses
of the same trials. Across those, the number of hypotheses is not well defined, and the
positive-dependence condition that licenses Benjamini--Hochberg under dependence cannot
be established. A false-discovery rate computed over such a family is not interpretable.
The three properties' pooled time-courses rest on disjoint sets of trials, and correcting
each property's family separately keeps every family self-contained.`r decode_status_appendix()`

# Retention contrasts in full {#apx-retention-tables}

The Results report the retention contrasts that carry the argument. The two tables below
give the full record: every Session 4 to Session 6 contrast of the reported ERP and accuracy
models (@tbl-retention), and every retention-free contrast from the refits that carry an
explicit retention indicator (@tbl-retention-free). Both are read from the pooled contrast
artefact and reproduce with it.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-retention
#| tbl-cap: "Session 4 to Session 6 Retention Contrasts"
#| apa-note: "Each contrast is the change in the grammaticality effect across the retention interval: posterior median, 95% credible interval and probability of direction, overall, within each language and for the between-language difference (Mini-Norwegian minus Mini-English). The two model families are on different scales, as the Measure column records. ERP contrasts are in within-participant SD units of amplitude and accuracy contrasts in log-odds, so medians should be compared only within a measure. Dashes in the window and region columns mark the accuracy models, which are fitted per property and have neither. For compactness, Gender means subject--verb gender agreement, Object marking means differential object marking, and Number agreement means verb--object number agreement."
#| apa-longtable: true
#| tbl-colwidths: [18, 11, 9, 9, 18, 10, 19, 6]
if (!is.null(retention_tbl) && has_knitr) {
  # As with the forest plot, restrict to the reported fits: the artefact carries all four
  # variants of every cell and printing it whole put a 225-row table in the middle of the
  # Results, in which the reported rows were indistinguishable from the sensitivity ones.
  rtb <- retention_tbl |>
    filter(!grepl("_weakprior", model), !grepl("_retfree", model),
           model == vapply(sub("_itemslope$", "", model), .mid, ""))
  # Precision is uniform within each model family (ERP rows, accuracy rows), so a reader
  # can compare down a column; see .fmt_est.
  .f <- .fmt_est(rtb$median, rtb$ci_low, rtb$ci_high, group = grepl("^erp_", rtb$model))
  rt <- cbind(.retention_labels(rtb),
              data.frame(Median = .f$median, `95% CrI` = .f$ci,
                         `$p_d$` = .fmt_pd(rtb$pd),
                         check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  rt <- rt[order(rt$Property, rt$`Window (ms)`, rt$Region, rt$Contrast), ]
  knitr::asis_output("\\Needspace{12\\baselineskip}\n")
  knitr::kable(rt, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r"))
} else {
  cat("*Retention contrasts will appear here once the models are fitted.*")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-retention-free
#| tbl-cap: "Retention-Free Contrasts From the Refits Carrying an Explicit Retention Indicator"
#| apa-note: "Each contrast is the deviation of the grammaticality effect at Session 6 from the trend established across the training sessions: posterior median, 95% credible interval and probability of direction, overall, within each language and for their difference (Mini-Norwegian minus Mini-English). All estimates are in within-participant SD units of amplitude. Verb--object number agreement is omitted because its indicator is not identifiable. For compactness, Gender means subject--verb gender agreement and Object marking means differential object marking."
#| apa-longtable: true
#| tbl-colwidths: [18, 11, 9, 18, 10, 28, 6]
if (!is.null(retention_tbl) && has_knitr) {
  want_item <- identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")
  rtf <- retention_tbl |>
    filter(grepl("_retfree", model), !grepl("_weakprior", model),
           grepl("_itemslope", model) == want_item)
  if (nrow(rtf)) {
    .f <- .fmt_est(rtf$median, rtf$ci_low, rtf$ci_high)
    lb <- .retention_labels(rtf)
    lb$Measure <- NULL              # a single measure here, so the column carries nothing
    rf <- cbind(lb, data.frame(Median = .f$median, `95% CrI` = .f$ci,
                               `$p_d$` = .fmt_pd(rtf$pd),
                               check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
    rf <- rf[order(rf$Property, rf$`Window (ms)`, rf$Region, rf$Contrast), ]
    knitr::asis_output("\\Needspace{12\\baselineskip}\n")
    knitr::kable(rf, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r"))
  } else {
    cat("*Retention-free contrasts will appear here once the refit is pooled.*")
  }
} else {
  cat("*Retention-free contrasts will appear here once the models are fitted.*")
}
```

# Prior specifications {#apx-prior-specifications}

The reasoning behind each prior is given in the Method, under *Priors*. What follows is the
specification itself. Every mean and standard deviation is on the standardised scale, so a
coefficient is in standard-deviation units, within participant for the ERP models. Prior
means encode a direction and a regularised magnitude only, never a literature effect size,
because the sources do not supply a transferable one. A directional prior is placed only
where the literature supports a sign. Everything else, including the grammaticality slope
in the 200--500 ms window, differential object marking at 300--600 ms, the hemisphere
interactions and the transfer interaction under test, takes the model's zero-centred
default.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-priors
#| tbl-cap: "Prior Distributions Placed on Each Parameter"
#| apa-note: "Zero-centred entries carry no directional claim. The standard deviation is what bounds the prior's influence. The weakly informative baseline used for the sensitivity analysis replaces every informative mean below with zero and widens the corresponding standard deviation."
# Generated by calling the same prior builders the models were fitted with, rather than
# transcribed. les_erp_prior() and les_acc_prior() in _shared/R/01_bayesian_settings.R are
# pure functions of (property, window, macroregion), so the table cannot drift from the
# fitted specification: change a prior there and this table changes with it. Transcribing
# them by hand had already introduced three wrong values, because a directional prior is
# emitted only where its mean is non-zero and the zero-centred cases fall back to the class
# default, which reading the prose did not reveal.
.priors_ok <- has_knitr && requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE) &&
  file.exists(here::here("_shared", "R", "01_bayesian_settings.R"))
if (.priors_ok) {
  # The settings file announces the backend and threading with cat(), which chunk options
  # cannot suppress because it is printed output rather than a message; unwrapped, that
  # banner rendered as a stray line of console text in this appendix.
  invisible(utils::capture.output(suppressPackageStartupMessages(
    source(here::here("_shared", "R", "01_bayesian_settings.R")))))
  .fmt <- function(x) {
    x <- sub("^normal\\(", "N(", x)
    x <- sub("^student_t\\(", "t(", x)
    sub("^lkj\\(", "LKJ(", x)
  }
  .label <- function(coef, class) {
    if (class == "sd")        return("Random-effect standard deviations")
    if (class == "sigma")     return("Residual standard deviation")
    if (class == "cor")       return("Random-effect correlations")
    if (class == "Intercept") return("Intercept")
    if (!nzchar(coef))        return("All remaining coefficients")
    coef <- gsub("^z_recoded_", "", coef)
    # A literal multiplication sign, not "$\\times$": the backslash of a maths
    # replacement string is consumed by gsub, so the cell rendered as "$times$".
    lab <- gsub("z_recoded_", "", gsub(":", " x ", coef))
    # Match the sentence case of the class labels above, which are capitalised.
    paste0(toupper(substr(lab, 1, 1)), substr(lab, 2, nchar(lab)))
  }
  # Walk the grid the models were actually fitted over.
  .rows <- list()
  for (p in names(LES_P1_PROPERTIES)) for (w in c("200_500", "300_600", "400_900")) {
    d <- as.data.frame(les_erp_prior(property = p, window = w, macroregion = "lateral"))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(d))) {
      .rows[[length(.rows) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
        model = "ERP", coef = d$coef[i], class = d$class[i], prior = d$prior[i],
        where = sprintf("%s ms, %s", sub("_", "--", w), gsub("_", " ", p)),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
  for (p in names(LES_P1_PROPERTIES)) {
    d <- as.data.frame(les_acc_prior(property = p))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(d))) {
      .rows[[length(.rows) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
        model = "Accuracy", coef = d$coef[i], class = d$class[i], prior = d$prior[i],
        where = "accuracy models", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
  pr <- do.call(rbind, .rows)
  pr$Parameter <- mapply(.label, pr$coef, pr$class)
  # Describe a set of (window, property) cells in the terms the Method uses, rather than
  # listing every combination: the two agreement properties share a specification that
  # differential object marking does not, and that contrast is the point.
  .describe <- function(v) {
    v <- unique(v)
    if (length(v) >= 9L) return("all ERP models")
    # Accuracy rows carry a plain label, not a "window, property" pair; leave them alone.
    if (!any(grepl(", ", v, fixed = TRUE))) return(paste(sort(v), collapse = "; "))
    parts <- strsplit(v, ", ", fixed = TRUE)
    win <- vapply(parts, `[`, "", 1L); prop <- vapply(parts, `[`, "", 2L)
    paste(vapply(unique(win), function(w) {
      ps <- sort(unique(prop[win == w]))
      lab <- if (length(ps) == 3L) "all properties"
             else if (setequal(ps, c("gender agreement", "verb object number agreement")))
               "agreement properties"
             else paste(ps, collapse = " and ")
      paste0(w, ", ", lab)
    }, ""), collapse = "; ")
  }
  # One row per distinct (parameter, prior): a prior shared by every cell is stated once,
  # and one that varies by window or property names the cells it applies to.
  agg <- aggregate(where ~ Parameter + model + prior, data = pr, FUN = .describe)
  agg <- agg[order(agg$model != "ERP", agg$Parameter), ]
  out <- data.frame(Parameter = agg$Parameter,
                    `Model or window` = agg$where,
                    Prior = .fmt(agg$prior),
                    check.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(out, row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("*Prior specifications are generated from `_shared/R/01_bayesian_settings.R`",
      "and appear here when brms is available.*")
}
```

# Convergence diagnostics {#apx-convergence-diagnostics}

This appendix reports the realised sampling diagnostics for every fitted model. Each of
the 18 ERP cells was fitted under two random-effect structures (base and maximal) and
two prior sets, the literature-derived informative priors reported throughout and the
weakly informative baseline used for the sensitivity analysis, giving
`r conv_n("^erp_.*(lateral|midline)(_weakprior)?(_itemslope)?$")` grid fits. Each of the
3 accuracy models was fitted under the two prior sets alone, having a single
random-effect structure because no by-item term is carried, giving
`r conv_n("^accuracy_[a-z_]+(_weakprior)?$")` fits. The retention-free refits add
`r conv_n("_retfree$")` fits, the 12 gender-agreement and differential-object-marking
cells under both structures with the informative
priors.`r if (!is.null(conv_tbl) && any(grepl("_keepmisfiltered|_diversity", conv_tbl$model))) " The data-side sensitivity variants are marked in the table's own columns." else ""`
In all, `r if (is.null(conv_tbl)) "NN" else nrow(conv_tbl)` models were fitted.
@tbl-convergence-appendix gives the realised diagnostics for every one, so a
model that converged comfortably can be told from one that converged marginally.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-convergence-appendix
#| tbl-cap: "Convergence Diagnostics for Every Fitted Model"
#| apa-note: "Properties are abbreviated to keep the table within the measure: Gender is subject--verb gender agreement, Object marking is differential object marking, and Number agreement is verb--object number agreement. $\\widehat{R}$ is the maximum rank-normalised $\\widehat{R}$ and each ESS the minimum effective sample size, both taken over all parameters of the model. A blank window and region mark the grammaticality-judgement accuracy models, which are not resolved by time window or scalp region. The retention-free column marks the refits in which the Session-6 step is freed from the training trend. No model produced a divergent transition, and all met the criteria of $\\widehat{R}$ below 1.01 with both effective sample sizes above 400."
#| apa-longtable: true
#| tbl-colwidths: [15, 12, 10, 12, 13, 15, 7, 8, 8]
if (!is.null(conv_tbl) && has_knitr) {
  # Every variant lives in the model id as a suffix; split each into its own column so the
  # name column stays inside the measure and the grid is readable as a design rather than
  # as a list of run tags. Structure is read off the id rather than from the artefact's
  # `structure` column, which records "base" for the retention-free maximal refits even
  # though their ids carry "_itemslope"; the id is the field every other accessor in this
  # manuscript treats as authoritative for the random-effect structure.
  # The id packs the whole design into one underscore-joined token, e.g.
  # "differential_object_marking_200_500_lateral". Printed whole that is a single
  # unbreakable word: LaTeX cannot hyphenate it, so it overran its column and collided
  # with the next one. Split it into the three design fields it encodes, which fixes the
  # overflow because each field breaks at a space, and reads as a design rather than as a
  # run tag. Accuracy models carry no window or region and leave those cells empty.
  .stem <- conv_tbl$model |>
    sub("_keepmisfiltered", "", x = _) |>
    sub("_diversity", "", x = _) |>
    sub("_weakprior", "", x = _) |>
    sub("_itemslope", "", x = _) |>
    sub("_retfree", "", x = _) |>
    sub("^erp_", "", x = _) |>
    sub("^accuracy_", "", x = _)
  .cellpat <- "_([0-9]{3}_[0-9]{3})_(lateral|midline)$"
  .graded  <- grepl(.cellpat, .stem)
  # An id with no entry in the map keeps its stripped form rather than being dropped, so
  # a property added later still appears.
  # Short labels, spelled out in the note. Pandoc allocates each column a share of the
  # measure proportional to its widest cell, so the full names took 29% of the table and
  # squeezed "informative" in the Priors column until it overran into its neighbour.
  .propmap <- c(
    gender_agreement             = "Gender",
    differential_object_marking  = "Object marking",
    verb_object_number_agreement = "Number agr.")
  .prop <- ifelse(.graded, sub(.cellpat, "", .stem), .stem)
  ct <- conv_tbl |>
    transmute(
      Property = ifelse(is.na(.propmap[.prop]), gsub("_", " ", .prop),
                        unname(.propmap[.prop])),
       `Window (ms)` = ifelse(.graded,
                       sub("_", "--", sub(paste0("^.*", .cellpat), "\\1", .stem)),
                       ""),
      Region = ifelse(.graded,
                      unname(c(lateral = "Lateral", midline = "Midline")[
                        sub(paste0("^.*", .cellpat), "\\2", .stem)]),
                      ""),
      Structure = ifelse(grepl("_itemslope", model), "maximal", "base"),
      Priors    = if ("prior_variant" %in% names(conv_tbl)) prior_variant else NA_character_,
      `Retention-free` = ifelse(grepl("_retfree", model), "yes", "no"),
      # The two data-side sensitivity variants. Both columns collapse away below whenever
      # the variant has not been fitted, so the table is unchanged until one exists.
      `Mis-filtered retained` = ifelse(grepl("_keepmisfiltered", model), "yes", "no"),
      `Diversity covariate` = ifelse(grepl("_diversity", model), "yes", "no"),
      `$\\widehat{R}$` = round(max_rhat, 3),
      `ESS (bulk)` = round(min_ess_bulk),
      `ESS (tail)` = round(min_ess_tail))
  # Drop an identifying column only when it is constant, so the table never hides a
  # distinction that is actually present.
  if (all(ct$`Window (ms)` == "")) ct$`Window (ms)` <- NULL
  if (all(ct$Region == "")) ct$Region <- NULL
  if (all(is.na(ct$Structure)) || length(unique(ct$Structure)) == 1) ct$Structure <- NULL
  if (all(is.na(ct$Priors))    || length(unique(ct$Priors))    == 1) ct$Priors    <- NULL
  if (length(unique(ct$`Retention-free`)) == 1) ct$`Retention-free` <- NULL
  if (length(unique(ct$`Mis-filtered retained`)) == 1) ct$`Mis-filtered retained` <- NULL
  if (length(unique(ct$`Diversity covariate`)) == 1) ct$`Diversity covariate` <- NULL
  # Keep the short labels together in PDF output.  The wrappers are added only for
  # LaTeX; DOCX receives the ordinary text and therefore never exposes TeX markup.
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    ct$Region <- gsub("^Midline$", "\\\\mbox{Midline}", ct$Region)
    ct$Structure <- gsub("^maximal$", "\\\\mbox{maximal}", ct$Structure)
    ct$Priors <- gsub("^informative$", "\\\\mbox{informative}", ct$Priors)
    knitr::asis_output("\\Needspace{12\\baselineskip}\n")
    knitr::kable(ct, escape = FALSE)
  } else {
    knitr::kable(ct)
  }
} else {
  cat("*Convergence diagnostics will appear here once the models are fitted.*")
}
```

# Grand-average difference waves {#apx-difference-waves}

@fig-erp-difference plots the grand-average difference waves (grammatical minus
ungrammatical mean amplitude) at the same two sites as @fig-erp-waveforms. The two
displays summarise the same condition averages, so the difference waves are placed in
this appendix, where they aid legibility without adding information. Isolating the
difference makes the grammaticality effect visible where the overlaid condition waveforms
are dominated by the shared evoked response.

```{r}
#| label: fig-erp-difference
#| fig-cap: "Grand-Average Difference Waves per Property at the Two Representative Sites"
#| apa-note: "Difference waves are grammatical minus ungrammatical mean amplitude at the same two sites as the grand-average waveforms. Values above zero indicate a more positive amplitude on grammatical trials. Time zero is critical-word onset and the pre-stimulus baseline ($-100$ to 0 ms) is shaded, with window shading as in the waveform figure. The vertical axis is scaled separately for the two sites. These are descriptive condition averages with no uncertainty band, and the inferential statements come from the models. Like the waveforms, they are trial-weighted and computed on the full sample, including the four mis-filtered Session-3 datasets."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
if (length(ga_files) >= 6) {
  dsub <- ga[ga$brain_region %in% reps, c("grammatical_property", "grammaticality",
                                          "brain_region", "time", "mean_amp")]
  dg <- dplyr::rename(dplyr::filter(dsub, grammaticality == "Grammatical"),   gram = mean_amp)
  du <- dplyr::rename(dplyr::filter(dsub, grammaticality == "Ungrammatical"), ungram = mean_amp)
  dw <- dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(dg, -grammaticality),
                         dplyr::select(du, -grammaticality),
                         by = c("grammatical_property", "brain_region", "time"))
  dw$diff <- dw$gram - dw$ungram
  dw$Site <- factor(dw$brain_region, levels = reps,
                    labels = c("Midline posterior", "Left anterior"))
  dw$Property <- factor(dw$grammatical_property, levels = .props3)
  ggplot(dw, aes(time, diff)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -100, xmax = 0, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.35) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 200, xmax = 498, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.05, fill = "grey40") +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 300, xmax = 598, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.05, fill = "grey40") +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 400, xmax = 898, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.09, fill = "grey40") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey55") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey55") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.5, colour = "#0072B2") +
    facet_grid(Site ~ Property, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000)) +
    labs(x = "Time from critical-word onset (ms)",
         y = expression("Grammatical - ungrammatical (" * mu * "V, positive up)")) +
    les_theme()
}
```
